product_overview: MedChainID is a decentralized medical record verification platform leveraging the Aptos blockchain to enable privacy-first, tamper-resistant issuance and verification of one-time-use medical record tokens. It provides encrypted storage of medical documents on IPFS, secure token minting on the blockchain, patient-controlled sharing via secure links, and zero-knowledge verification by verifiers.
core_goals: Ensure all medical documents are securely encrypted before IPFS upload to protect patient privacy.
Provide issuers (hospitals, labs) with a seamless interface to mint tamper-proof medical record tokens on the Aptos blockchain.
Enable patients to view their medical records exclusively tied to their wallet addresses with robust filtering to prevent data leakage.
Facilitate secure sharing of medical records through verification links that embed decryption keys only in URL hash fragments for maximum security.
Allow verifiers to conduct zero-knowledge verification of medical records without decryption keys and enable one-time token consumption to prevent fraud.
Integrate optional machine learning service for fraud detection based on extracted document text analysis.
Build robust backend and frontend components ensuring error handling, validation, and scalability.
Comprehensively test edge cases and security vulnerabilities to protect against malformed inputs, unauthorized access, and blockchain transaction anomalies.
key_features: Medical Record Issuance: Hospitals and labs can upload medical documents which are encrypted and minted as tokens on the Aptos blockchain.
AES-256-CBC File Encryption: All uploaded documents are encrypted client-side before IPFS storage with a cryptographically secure key.
Blockchain Token Minting: Mint tokens containing document hash, IPFS CID, patient address, and record type on Aptos Devnet.
Patient Dashboard: Patients can view their own medical records filtered by their connected wallet address with protection against data leaks.
Secure Share Links: Generation of shareable verification URLs embedding decryption keys securely in URL hash fragments, preventing key exposure in server logs or network requests.
Zero-Knowledge Verification: Verifiers can view token metadata and verify document authenticity without access to encryption keys, and request decryption only if key is provided.
One-Time Token Consumption: Tokens are consumable once to prevent double-claiming and fraud in verification processes.
IPFS Storage via Pinata: Encrypted files are stored on IPFS with metadata for streamlined search and retrieval.
Optional ML Fraud Detection: An optional Python ML service analyzes document contents for fraud indicators during upload.
Comprehensive API Endpoints: Backend exposes secure endpoints for upload, decrypt, download, and verification supporting robust integrations.
user_flow_summary: Issuer Flow: Issuers upload encrypted medical documents via the frontend, specify record types and patient addresses, then mint blockchain tokens representing medical records.
Patient Flow: Patients connect their wallets, access a personalized dashboard displaying tokens filtered by their wallet address, and generate secure sharing links for medical records.
Verifier Flow: Verifiers use shared links containing IPFS CID and decryption keys in URL hash fragments to decrypt and view records or manually verify token validity without decryption keys.
Token Consumption Flow: Verified tokens can be consumed once by verifiers after blockchain transaction approval to prevent reuse or fraud.

Edge Case and Error Handling Flow: The system detects and gracefully handles invalid inputs, malformed IPFS CIDs, wrong decryption keys, wallet disconnections, and network errors, providing user-friendly feedback.
ML Fraud Detection Flow (Optional): Uploaded documents are processed by an ML service to analyze textual fraud markers, influencing risk analysis metadata attached to uploads.
validation_criteria: All uploaded files MUST be encrypted with AES-256-CBC before IPFS upload; failure to encrypt is a critical security defect.
Patient dashboard MUST only display records that match the connected wallet address; cross-patient data exposure is unacceptable.
Shareable URLs MUST embed decryption keys only in the URL hash fragment (#key=...), NOT in query parameters to avoid key leakage.
Decryption attempts with wrong keys MUST fail with error; no corrupted or partial data must be returned to ensure confidentiality.
Blockchain functions MUST correctly handle all relevant data fields, ensuring eight values (including patient address) are correctly parsed and managed without omission.
Token consumption MUST update blockchain state to prevent double-claiming, with UI reflecting the token's consumed status accurately.
API endpoints MUST validate input formats, reject malformed IPFS CIDs, and handle missing parameters gracefully with informative error messages.
The system MUST handle edge cases including file size limits, concurrent operations, wallet disconnections, and availability issues in IPFS and ML services without crashing.
Comprehensive manual and automated tests must cover critical, high, and medium priority edge cases and user journeys, ensuring robustness and security.
Encryption keys or sensitive information MUST never be leaked through URLs, network requests, or logs, adhering to strict security protocols.
Decryption and token verification workflows MUST handle missing, tampered, or invalid inputs gracefully, maintaining system integrity and user trust.

critical_security_features.description: Files MUST be encrypted (AES-256) before uploading to IPFS
Patient dashboard filters records by patient_address. Only records matching connected wallet are displayed

If URL has no #key= fragment, application MUST NOT attempt to decrypt
POST /api/decrypt-view MUST fail if wrong decryption key is provided
